reasoning.text: The render already passes both acceptance tests: ISO shows an open, fully populated eight-lane board with no opaque block swallowing a subsystem, TOP confirms all eight blue BRAM banks, the copper DSP multiplier column as a vertical row of dots, the cylindrical Barrett spine plus the boxy shift/subtract member, the brass twiddle feeder L, both white FIFOs, and the seven-fin exploded heatsink; SIDE shows the exploded butterfly lane riding on its risers. The carried-over gaps (8 BUs, cylindrical Barrett) are now closed in the input scene. The two real weaknesses left are geometric: the butterfly array is still one monolithic open plate rather than a frame of real members, and the elevated return bus floats over the array in the SIDE/FRONT elevations with no visible standoff. There is also a minor annotation inconsistency — the exploded heatsink's role claims it cools the DSP array while it sits over the right-edge control cluster.
gaps: Add short standoff posts under the twiddle broadcast rail and the read bus as well (only the return bus is grounded now) so all three overhead routing channels are supported in the elevation views and the read/twiddle/return triad reads as physical wiring rather than floating lines

Consider moving the exploded heatsink stack slightly toward the array center (x ~2) so its die-coverage claim is spatially closer to the logic it cools, but only if it can be done without the lifted fins occluding the multiplier column in ISO

Verify against the next render that the new low side rails (height 0.5 m) do not visually merge with the dark reduction spine in TOP; if they do, recolor the rails to a lighter brushed steel to keep the open frame legible

fields.before: Single open mounting baseplate spanning all eight parallel butterfly lanes, exposing every DSP multiplier and symmetric add/sub operator from above (X-ray cutaway).
fields.after: Thin open floor of the butterfly-array frame; together with the two longitudinal rails and the cross-brace it forms an open chassis spanning all eight parallel lanes, exposing every DSP multiplier and symmetric add/sub operator from above (X-ray cutaway).

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Lay one shared open butterfly-array baseplate across the array, then populate it with eight parallel butterfly clusters (one per BRAM bank); inside each cluster wire the DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar, and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
meta.after: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
